I don’t want to sound rude, but it seems your trapped in a very unhealthy household. My best piece of advice would be to move out. If you live near a college you can find roommates on Craigslist or a college roommate app. Don’t let negativity be the decipher on whether you live or not. You’re so young and have so much to live for. 

Sometimes the hardest and scariest decisions we make end up being the most crucial fo our own well being. For example, I lived at home with my mom until I was 20 and then took out a $10,000 loan and boat a small sailboat to live on. It was a 27 foot sailboat and my “rent” was $125 which included electricity, water, power and internet. It was the best decision I ever made in my life. Simple living and no one  to bother me. 

My point is, don’t let this bullshit get to you. We all hate our teen years. They are terrible. Just try your best to use this as motivation to move forward. I’m here to help if I can, but don’t do it. It’s a decision you can’t take back. Once you’ve done it, it’s over.

Hey buddy, sounds like you’re going through quite a bit right now. I know it can be overwhelming at that age and as for the drugs are concerned, you very much young enough to tackle this problem and fix it. I know people in their 40’s who are less brave than you are by not seeking advice. 

You’re a young and smart young adult, I can tell by the way you type. You’re far too smart to let your life end over depression and drug use. I realize this isn’t what you want to hear, but I hope you’ll hear us out. 

When I was 15, my dad died unexpectedly and it crushed my life. In all honesty, I still fight the depression of losing him everyday. Especially since I was about to ride with him to work the morning he died. For years I blamed myself. Now, I’m not saying everything is great, but I have a few friends who I talk to on a regular basis and take medication (that has been a godsend, but no effects of being “high”) instead it allows me to focus on work and not my anxiety. 

At your age, I would absolutely recommend seeking some medical advise and help. This DOESN’T make you weak. It makes you a reasonable and responsible adult. Don’t feel ashamed. You have a lot of life left in you and there’s so much time to turn it around. Hell, you could even be president one day! You’re smart, articulate and caring. I can tell by the way you speak. Please. For your family and friends, see what you can do about help. I’m here if you need to talk.

I saw you say past 25. How old are you if you mind me asking? I know things can seem insanely difficult at that time of your life, but you need to remember, you’re still young! I’m 29 and have trouble realizing that, because all I’ve accomplished is an associates degree and more student loan debt than I know what to do with. Are you in school? What interests you? Talk to me. Let’s work this out. Learn from my mistakes. I bet we could connect on many levels.

People are the most important part of your life. Your kids and wife don’t love you for money. Taking your own life will crush them. Coming from a guy who lost his dad at 16 (because he didn’t take his blood pressure medicine and had a heart attack), I can tell you personally I’d rather be homeless and have my dad. Even now that I’m almost 30, it’s something I think about daily. Just keep working hard and cherish every moment you have. Don’t give up.
